newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-WE HAD TO DIG DEEP TO WIN - LIONS SKIPPER.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WE HAD TO DIG DEEP TO WIN - LIONS SKIPPER.

text.p: British Lions skipper Martin Johnson said he had never been in as tough a match in his northern hemisphere career as his side's 38-21 win over Western Province on Saturday.
"That was tougher than anything I have ever had in the Five Nations, full stop," said Johnson, who was playing his first match on tour after missing the opening two victories.
"It was tremendously quick, the skill levels were very high from both sides. Western Province scrummaged extremely strongly and we had to play well and dig deep to win.
"Sometimes in the Five Nations you have the same pace of game but not the same concentration or the same skill with it.
"They can play a very quick game here and stay in control of the ball. It's very difficult to get the ball back off sides here."
Johnson, a veteran of 30 England tests, suffered the indignity of seeing a Lions pack featuring seven of England's Triple Crown pack being shunted backwards.
"They scrummaged tremendously well as a team while we scrummaged as individuals and it's something we will have to work on," said Johnson.
Western Province captain Dick Muir, who scored two of his side's three tries, said he was impressed by the Lions.
"I didn't expect them to play as fast a game and I was really impressed by their handling skills.
"One of the players that stood out to me was Gregor Townsend. He varied it very well: took it deep, took it flat, he created play for his centres."
